Quick answer: install the free WP Job Manager plugin, create three pages (Jobs, Post a Job and Job Dashboard), and add a shortcode to each: [jobs], [submit_job_form] and [job_dashboard]. That gives you searchable job listings, front-end job submission and an employer dashboard. Paid add-ons (from $29 a year) add applications, paid listings, job alerts and more.

Key takeaways

  • WP Job Manager is a free plugin made by Automattic and works with most themes.
  • It suits both a simple careers page for your own business and a full job board where employers post jobs.
  • Listings include Google job schema, which helps them appear in job search results.
  • Add-ons cost from $29 to $79 a year each, or all core add-ons in a bundle from $159 a year.
Quick pick

Adding job listings to your site? Get WP Job Manager →

Careers page or job board: which do you need?

WP Job Manager handles both. A careers page is the quickest win: it gives job seekers a page on your own domain instead of only third-party job sites.

What does the free WP Job Manager plugin include?

  • Searchable, filterable listings by keyword, location, category and job type.
  • Front-end forms so employers (or you) can submit and preview jobs without the admin area.
  • A jobs dashboard where logged-in employers manage their listings and see views.
  • Apply options: each job can use an application email address or a link to an external form.
  • Google job schema, so search engines can read your listings.
  • RSS feeds of jobs.

Its WordPress.org page showed 70,000+ active installations and a 4.4 out of 5 rating when we checked, and it was updated in November 2026.

How to set up WP Job Manager: step by step

  1. Install the plugin. Plugins → Add New, search for “WP Job Manager”, install and activate. The setup wizard can create the pages for you.
  2. Create the Jobs page. Add a page called “Jobs” (or “Careers”) and insert a Shortcode block containing [jobs].
  3. Create the Post a Job page (job boards only). Add a page with [submit_job_form] for front-end submissions.
  4. Create the Job Dashboard page (job boards only). Add a page with [job_dashboard] so logged-in employers can manage listings.
  5. Review the settings. Under Job Listings → Settings, choose listings per page, whether categories and job types are on, who can post, whether new jobs need your approval and how long listings last.
  6. Add categories and job types such as Full-time, Part-time and Contract.
  7. Post a test job, check it on desktop and mobile, then publish your real openings.
  8. Add the Jobs page to your menu and link it from your About or Contact page.

The official shortcode reference also says not to wrap shortcodes in other tags. In the block editor, use a Shortcode block.

Useful shortcode options

Which paid add-ons are worth it?

These are the “from” prices on WP Job Manager’s core add-ons page in November 2026 (single-site licenses with a year of updates and support):

Our suggestion: for a careers page, start free and add Applications only if you want applications kept in WordPress instead of email. For a paid job board, start with Simple Paid Listings (or WC Paid Listings if you already run WooCommerce) plus Job Alerts. WP Job Manager offers refunds within 14 days of purchase.

Tips for a job board that works

  • Require approval for new listings so spam does not go live.
  • Set listings to expire (for example after 30 days) so old jobs do not linger.
  • Write clear titles (“Part-time Dental Receptionist, Austin”) and include pay where you can.
  • Applications contain personal data: use HTTPS, keep WordPress updated, and see our secure form guide.
  • Check your listings in Google Search Console after launch; our Search Console guide shows how.

WP Job Manager pros and cons

FAQ

Is WP Job Manager free?

Yes. The core plugin is free on WordPress.org. Paid add-ons extend it.

Will my jobs show up in Google job search?

WP Job Manager adds Google job schema to listings, which makes them eligible. Google decides what it shows, so follow its job posting guidelines and keep listings current.

Can I charge employers to post jobs?

Yes, with the Simple Paid Listings add-on (Stripe or PayPal) or WC Paid Listings (WooCommerce).

Does it work with my theme?

It is shortcode-based and works with most themes, sometimes with small CSS tweaks. Some themes are built specifically for WP Job Manager.

Can candidates upload a resume?

With the Applications add-on candidates can apply on your site, and Resume Manager lets them submit full resumes.

Conclusion

For a careers page, the free WP Job Manager plugin and one Jobs page with [jobs] are all you need. For a full job board, add the submission and dashboard pages, require approval, and add paid listings and job alerts when you are ready to earn from it. Prices and features were checked on the vendors’ official pages in November 2026. They change, so confirm on the vendor’s site before you buy.
